battle.name: 李子通起義
battle.theater: 東海郡嶧縣至海陵江都
battle.brief: 大業十一年（615），東海郡嶧縣漁戶出身的李子通在山東聚眾，先與左才相合勢，後附杜伏威，武德二年在海陵自立，破陳稜而克江都，稱帝建吳。卡面這件羅馬短劍屬刺擊型近身短兵，隋軍與義軍真正貼身纏鬥的則是環首刀與匕首，刺突與劈砍的節奏才是這場戰爭的收尾。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 這場起義的交戰雙方，先是隋朝與山東的流民武裝，後是隋朝及其崩解後的割據者，與李子通自己建立的吳國。隋朝一方是中央與州郡兩層體系：中央以煬帝為核心，宿衛分殿內四衛（驃騎、翊衛、武賁、虎賁）與各類郎將，州郡則置刺史、太守、縣令，各郡有郡兵、各縣有縣兵，徵發與調配全靠文書往返；大業十一年（615）煬帝正在遼東柳城與突厥、句麗周旋，江都一線只留留守府與漕轉機構維持。起義一方起初沒有編制：李子通與左才相合勢，靠的是漁戶、船戶與山東的流民，加上一批逃戶、逃卒，既無軍餉也無官爵，只靠分食與散財聚人，數月之間拉起數千至數萬量級的隊伍。他一度附於杜伏威，接受了淮南義軍那套設軍令、行賞罰、按小隊作戰的做法；自立於海陵後，才有自己的名號、戶口與鹽利收入，可以供數萬人的船兵吃糧。第三方自始至終在場：河北的竇建德、江淮的杜伏威、洛陽的王世充與東都楊侗，以及武德年間接手的唐朝。619年李子通克江都、自稱皇帝建吳，隋朝在江淮的實際控制便只剩留守府與幾處據點；到620年，竇建德與杜伏威兩面逼近，唐朝也以援軍的名義把手伸進了這條運河。命令體系方面，義軍靠口傳與旗幟，隋軍靠軍令文書與宿衛編制，唐軍則以行軍總管與偏師制運作，三套指揮鏈在江淮的水網與運河上互相摩擦。
countriesEn: The two sides of this rebellion were, at first, the Sui state and an armed band of displaced men in Shandong; later, the Sui and the powers that emerged from its collapse; and finally the Sui against the state of Wu that Li Zitong founded himself. The Sui side worked on two levels. At the centre stood Emperor Yang, with the palace guards divided into the Four Guards of the Household — the Piaojun, Yijun, Wubei and Huben — together with a range of langjiang officers; below that, each commandery and county had its own governor, administrator and magistrate, and each commandery kept commandery troops while each county kept county troops, with mustering and shifting done entirely through written orders. In 615 Emperor Yang was himself in Liucheng in Liaodong, grinding against the Turks and Goguryeo, so in Jiangdu only a garrison headquarters and the grain-ferry apparatus were left to hold the line. The insurgents had no establishment at the start. When Li Zitong joined forces with Zuo Caixiang what he had to offer was fishermen, boatmen and the displaced of Shandong, together with deserters and runaways, with neither pay nor rank but shared meals and scattered money; within months he had raised a following in the thousands and stretching towards tens of thousands. He attached himself for a time to Du Fuwei and took over the way the Huainan insurgents ran their business — set up military orders, pay and discipline, and fight in small detachments — and only after establishing himself at Hailing did he have a title, registers and salt revenue enough to feed tens of thousands of boat soldiers. Third parties were present throughout: Dou Jiande in Hebei, Du Fuwei in the Huai and Yangtze delta, Wang Shichong and the emperor Yang Tong at Luoyang, and the Tang court, which took over in the Wu-de era. When Li Zitong took Jiangdu in 619 and proclaimed himself emperor of Wu, all that remained of Sui control south of the Yangtze was a few garrisons; by 620 Dou Jiande and Du Fuwei were closing in from two sides, and the Tang had extended a hand into the canal under the guise of a relief army. Orders moved by word of mouth and by flags in the rebel camp, by written dispatch and register system in the Sui ranks, and by travelling commanders with detached wings in the Tang army; all three chains of command ground against each other along the waterways and canals of the Huai region.
people: 核心人物是李子通（？—622），東海郡（今山東嶧縣）人，漁民出身，早年以小吏起家，輕財好施，在漁戶與船戶之中頗得人心。大業末年他先在山東聚眾，與泰山、濟北一帶的群盜首領左才相合勢；隨著他名望漸高，左才相心生猜忌，李子通便脫隊而去，轉投淮南最大的義軍首領杜伏威。杜伏威比李子通年長近二十歲，旗下有輔公祏等一批死黨，在淮南打了七年游擊，把隋朝在江淮的郡兵拖得精疲力竭。李子通在其麾下待了一段時間，學會了不與隋軍主力硬碰的小隊流動作戰，也看見了江淮鹽區與運河物資的分量；後來他脫離杜伏威，在海陵（今江蘇泰州）自立，把漁戶出身的優勢變成水軍。隋方與割據方的關鍵人物同樣在場：隋煬帝楊廣三征高句麗，615年九月在雁門被突厥包圍，靠義軍與裴矩之謀才脫身，618年三月在江都被宇文化及所弒；竇建德是河北最大的義軍首領，618年稱帝、621年在虎牢關敗於唐軍被擒；洛陽方面是王世充把持朝政、楊侗為帝；杜伏威於619年歸唐，封吳王、賜姓李。真正扭轉局面的，是唐方的秦叔寶：武德四年正月，他率軍邀擊竇建德於泗州一線、毀其舟師，李子通的江淮才沒有被兩面夾擊吞掉。李子通本人於武德五年（622）卒於長安，其吳國隨之瓦解。
peopleEn: The central figure is Li Zitong (d. 622), a native of Donghai commandery, present-day Yixian in Shandong, the son of a fisherman who began as a minor clerk and was known for giving away what he had, which in the fishing and boat communities of the coast bought him a following. Late in the Daye era he first gathered men in Shandong and joined forces with Zuo Caixiang, the bandit chief who commanded a band around Mount Tai and northern Jibei. As Li's own reputation grew, Zuo grew jealous of it, and Li left the alliance and turned instead to Du Fuwei, the strongest of the southern insurgents. Du Fuwei was nearly twenty years older and had at his side men like Fu Gongshi; for seven years he had worn the Sui down in the Huai valley, always avoiding the Sui's main body and hitting the detachments. In Du's camp Li Zitong learned the tactics of small, fluid bands and saw what the salt pans and the canal traffic of the Huai-Tai region were worth; later he broke with Du and set up on his own at Hailing, present-day Taizhou in Jiangsu, turning his fisherman's background into a water force. The other decisive figures belong to the Sui side and to the neighbouring powers. Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, had campaigned against Goguryeo three times, was trapped by the Turks at Yanmen in the ninth month of 615 and released only after the intervention of his volunteers and the diplomacy of Pei Ju, and was murdered at Jiangdu by Yuwen Huaji in the third month of 618. Dou Jiande, the largest rebel leader in Hebei, proclaimed himself emperor in 618 and was taken prisoner after his defeat at Hulao Pass in 621. At Luoyang, Wang Shichong held the real power while Yang Tong sat on the throne. Du Fuwei submitted to the Tang in 619, was made Prince of Wu and granted the surname Li. The man who actually turned the tables was Qin Shubao of the Tang: in the first month of 621 he caught Dou Jiande near Si prefecture and destroyed his river fleet, and only then was Li Zitong's position in the Huai saved from being pinched from both sides. Li himself died at Chang'an in 622, and the state of Wu broke apart with him.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬短劍是刺擊型近身短兵：雙刃直脊、握柄貼合掌心，羅馬人把它留給戰線塌陷之後的最後一段白刃，靠盾的邊緣護住刺出的那一刺。本場戰爭裡沒有它的原型——隋的軍械譜系裡不存在羅馬短劍——但它對應的裝備位置卻是實在的：李子通的義軍步卒大多無重甲，靠短刀、匕首與木皮盾在船板、岸灘、鹽場棧橋和城門甬道裡貼身互刺，刺突的節奏與盾沿的掩護就是這支部隊的全部武藝。與之相配的還有削尖的竹木矛、標槊、環首刀、環首錐、鐵叉、角弓與竹木弓、少量蹶張弩，護具多為皮甲、札甲碎片與兜鍪，鎧甲只有被繳獲的隋軍才有。江淮是水鄉，舟師就是義軍的正規軍：平底沙船、艤板與改裝的漁船組成運輸隊，攻江都靠的是船隊包抄與斷糧，登岸則靠輕裝步兵。隋軍那邊是另一套：明光甲、長槊與方陣步卒、弓弩手、櫓車與撞車，攻城有雲梯、飛石與巢車，江都的漕運船隊裡還有煬帝造的巨型樓船。鹽是李子通最重要的裝備性物資——海陵一帶的鹽場產出可換米、換布、換兵器的硬貨；馬匹則是他早期的稀缺品：山東尚能繳獲與徵集，轉入江淮後騎兵比例驟降，逼他把作戰重心從陸路挪到水面。
kitsEn: The card shows a Roman gladius, a thrusting side-arm of close combat: a double-edged blade with a straight spine and a grip that sits in the palm, a weapon the Romans held back for the last stretch of a collapsing line, relying on the edge of the shield to cover the thrust. There is no prototype of it in this war — no Roman short sword appears in any Sui ordnance inventory — but the place it occupies in the order of battle is nonetheless real. Li Zitong's foot soldiers mostly had no heavy armour. They fought with short swords, daggers and wooden or hide-covered shields, stabbing at one another on plank decking, along the shore, on the salt-pan causeways and inside the gates and passages of a city, and the rhythm of the thrust with the shelter of the shield rim was the whole of their martial art. Beside these went sharpened bamboo and wooden spears, ji spear-staves, ring-pommel swords and ring-pommel awls, iron forks, antler bows and bamboo-wood bows, a few crossbows; armour was limited to hide coats, fragments of lamellar plate and helmets, and plate mail existed only on the Sui soldiers who had been captured. The Huai region was a country of water, so the boat force was the rebels' real army: flat-bottomed sand boats, side punts and converted fishing craft made up the transport fleet; the assault on Jiangdu was carried by ships moving in to close the water and cut the grain, and the landing was made by lightly equipped infantry. The Sui system was different: bright plate, long spears and ranked spearmen, bow and crossbowmen, mantlets and battering rams, with ladders, stone-throwers and siege towers for the attack on a city, and in the grain fleet that served Jiangdu the giant tower ships built by Emperor Yang. Salt was the most important supply item Li Zitong held — the output of the pans around Hailing was hard currency exchangeable for rice, cloth and iron. Horses were his scarcest possession, available in Shandong by capture and requisition but scarce once he was in the Huai, where the share of cavalry fell sharply and pushed the centre of gravity of his war off the roads and onto the water.
tactics: 起義的前半段靠地形和人心。山東沂水、濰水一帶的漁戶既靠水也靠田，隋朝的役使、鹽法與荒年把人逼到江邊，於是聚義的時候，來的首先不是步卒而是船戶：李子通的隊伍天生帶水軍色彩，能在白沙河道裡轉移，能靠夜航避開郡兵巡哨。附於杜伏威的幾年間，他把淮南義軍的打法學到手：不與隋軍主力硬碰，只打分遣出城的小股部隊，打完即退，轉入水網或山區，並用火攻與船隊切斷運河上的糧道。自立海陵之後，戰術重心換成守鹽與斷漕：控制鹽場等於握有養兵的財源，控制邗溝與淮水等於握有江淮的動脈，隋軍的糧船由洛陽、汴州沿運河北下，補給線一被切斷，留在江南的郡兵撐不過一季。619年攻江都，他以船隊封住水道、逼陳稜出城，盡量避免硬撞城牆；白刃相接最密集的地方，是城門、甬道與碼頭的跳板，那裡正是環首刀與匕首最常派上用場的場合。620年之後形勢逆轉，竇建德自河北沿運河南下，杜伏威自淮南西向，李子通只剩江都與數縣之地，只能節節依託運河與運河上的水寨死守，同時派使向唐請援。轉機出現在武德四年正月：秦叔寶率唐軍邀擊竇建德於泗州一線，毀其舟船，北方援軍既失水師又失銳氣，李子通才算把江都保了下來；此後他的軍隊便在唐與杜伏威、竇建德三方的夾縫裡維持殘局。
tacticsEn: The first half of the rebellion turned on terrain and on people. In the valleys of the Yi and Wei rivers in Shandong, fisher households lived off water and field at once, and the Sui's corvée, salt regulations and poor harvests pushed people down to the waterways, so when men gathered under a banner the first to come were not infantry but boatmen. Li Zitong's following was waterborne from the start, able to shift along the sand-choked channels and to move by night past the patrols of the commandery troops. During the years he spent under Du Fuwei he absorbed the southern way of fighting: never to collide with the main body of the Sui army, but to pick off the small detachments sent out of the cities, break away at once, and disappear into the water country or the hills, cutting the grain traffic on the canal with fire and with boats. Once he stood on his own at Hailing, the centre of his strategy changed to holding the salt pans and cutting the grain traffic. Control of the pans meant control of the money that fed the army; control of the Hangou canal and the Huai meant control of the artery of the region. The Sui grain fleet came down from Luoyang and Bianzhou along the canal, and once that supply line was cut the county troops left in the south could not last a season. In 619 he moved against Jiangdu with his fleet, closed the water and forced Chen Leng out into the open rather than smashing his head against the walls. The places where hand-to-hand fighting was thickest were the gates, the passages and the plank landings of the jetty, and there the ring-pommel sword and the dagger did their work. After 620 the tide turned: Dou Jiande came down from Hebei along the canal and Du Fuwei moved west from the Huai, leaving Li Zitong with Jiangdu and a few counties, so that he could only hold on stage by stage along the canal and the water forts on it, while sending envoys to ask the Tang for help. The opening came in the first month of 621, when Qin Shubao caught Dou Jiande near Si prefecture and destroyed his boats; the northern relief army lost both its river force and its momentum, and Li Zitong only then saved Jiangdu. After that his army merely held on in the gap between the Tang on one side and Du Fuwei and Dou Jiande on the other.
data: 可核對的數字不多，以下幾項大致可靠而須分清層次。大業十一年（615）九月，隋煬帝在雁門被突厥包圍，城中兵民約十五萬、存糧只支二十日、被圍約五十日，十五歲的李世民在募兵中隨援軍到城下；同年十一月煬帝自柳城北還，江都的漕運線再次吃緊。背景數字更駭人：大業八年第一次征高句麗，諸軍總計一百一十三萬人，渡河者三十萬五千，士卒死者十之八九，歸國者不過二三千，這一次大敗把隋朝能用的精騎與府庫積蓄耗在遼東。與本役直接相關的只有幾個節點：大業末年李子通先在山東聚眾；武德二年（619）破陳稜、克江都，自稱皇帝，國號吳，年號明政；武德三年（620）竇建德來攻，李子通遣使乞師於唐；武德四年（621）正月，秦叔寶邀擊竇建德於泗州，毀其舟師；武德五年（622）李子通卒於長安。里程上，東海郡嶧縣至海陵約六百餘里，海陵至江都沿邗溝約百二十里，義軍自嶧縣轉戰江淮的時間跨度因此拉得很長。兵員數字要特別當心：《隋書》未為李子通立傳，資治通鑑與兩《唐書》只留下數條散記，義軍兵眾只能說是數萬量級，江都守軍也只能按郡兵數千的量級理解，雙方死傷、攻城損失與繳獲一概沒有可核對的數字，不宜補造。
dataEn: Few numbers can be checked, and the ones that hold up only if the layers are kept apart. In the ninth month of 615 Emperor Yang was besieged by the Turks at Yanmen: the city held about 150,000 soldiers and people, its grain would serve twenty days, and the siege lasted some fifty days; fifteen-year-old Li Shimin came down with the recruited relief force. In the eleventh month the emperor turned north from Liucheng, and Jiangdu's grain route tightened again. The background figure is more shocking: for the first campaign against Goguryeo in 612 the Sui mustered 1,130,000 troops in all, of whom 305,000 crossed the river, and of the soldiers ten died for every one who survived, only two or three thousand returning home. That single defeat drained the empire's usable cavalry and its reserves in Liaodong. Only a few dates belong directly to this war: late in the Daye era Li Zitong first gathered men in Shandong; in 619, the second year of Wu-de, he defeated Chen Leng, took Jiangdu, proclaimed himself emperor, founded the state of Wu and adopted the era name Mingzheng; in 620, the third year of Wu-de, Dou Jiande attacked and Li Zitong sent an embassy to Tang to beg for troops; in the first month of 621 Qin Shubao caught Dou Jiande near Si prefecture and destroyed his fleet; in 622, the fifth year of Wu-de, Li Zitong died at Chang'an. As for distances: some six hundred li and more from Yixian in Donghai commandery to Hailing, and about a hundred and twenty li along the Hangou canal from Hailing to Jiangdu, so the insurgents' move from Shandong to the Huai was spread over a long stretch of time. The troop numbers must be handled carefully. The History of Sui devotes no biography to Li Zitong; the Comprehensive Mirror and the Old and New Tang histories each preserve only a few scattered notices. His following can only be called a following in the tens of thousands, and the Jiangdu garrison only a county force of a few thousand. There is no checkable figure for the losses on either side, for the cost of the sieges or for booty, and none should be invented.
cause: 四條線在615年的山東糾成一團。第一是兵：隋朝自大業六年起三次征高句麗，役夫、運丁與逃戶被編入軍籍與屯田，河北山東的丁壯大量脫離田畝，州郡手上的武裝既不精也不聽調。第二是饑與旱：山東連遭水旱，漁戶、鹽戶的生計被官府的鹽利與雜稅壓到斷絕，饒民大批流散，成為任何敢於舉旗者的人力。第三是隋廷的注意力全在北方：615年九月煬帝被突厥圍於雁門，十一月才自柳城北還，整個冬天帝國的注意力都在塞北與遼東，山東與江淮的郡兵只剩二流兵與臨時徵集的鄉勇。第四是人心：李子通輕財好施，散財於漁戶船戶之間，這在饑荒年月裡比任何官府的文書都管用；在他之前，王薄於611年在長平起事、竇建德於611年在漳州聚眾、張金稱在山東與河北轉戰五年，山東的盜風已成，李子通不過是接在同一條河道上的一支。到619年形勢再變：杜伏威在淮南已經打了六年，陳稜據江都掌著漕運與城防，李子通要的不是一場山林遭遇戰，而是江淮這塊能產鹽、能養船、能收漕糧的地盤；619年江都易主，隋朝在江南的樞紐便被生生挖去一角，而618年三月煬帝在江都被弒的消息，更讓所有人相信這個王朝撐不了多久。
causeEn: Four lines came together in Shandong in 615. First, men. From 606 the Sui had campaigned against Goguryeo three times, and corvée porters, transport levies and runaways were enrolled in the military registers and in the state farms, stripping the able-bodied from the fields of Hebei and Shandong; the arms the commanderies could raise were neither well drilled nor reliably responsive. Second, hunger and drought. Shandong suffered repeated floods and dry seasons, and the living of the fishing and salt households was crushed by the official salt revenues and the miscellaneous levies until it broke, so the displaced gathered in numbers and became the manpower of anyone prepared to raise a flag. Third, the court's whole attention was fixed to the north. In the ninth month of 615 Emperor Yang was shut up at Yanmen by the Turks and did not turn back from Liucheng until the eleventh, so through that winter the empire's attention was on the steppe and in Liaodong, and the commandery troops of Shandong and the Huai were second-rate soldiers and hastily mustered villagers. Fourth, hearts. Li Zitong gave away what he had, and in a year of famine that was worth more in Shandong than any government writ; by then the pattern was already set — Wang Bo had risen at Changping in 611, Dou Jiande had gathered men at Zhangzhou in 611, Zhang Jincheng had fought for five years through Shandong and Hebei — and Li Zitong was simply the next band on the same waterway. By 619 the picture had changed again. Du Fuwei had already spent six years in the Huai valley, Chen Leng held Jiangdu together with its grain traffic and its defences, and what Li Zitong was after was not a skirmish in the hills but the region that could produce salt, feed boats and collect grain. With Jiangdu changing hands in 619 the Sui lost a corner of its southern pivot, and the news that Emperor Yang had been killed at Jiangdu in the third month of 618 convinced everyone that the dynasty would not last.
impact: 直接影響有兩層。第一層是江淮的權力版圖：619年江都陷落，等於隋朝在江南的漕運樞紐與城防同時失守，江南的漕糧、鹽利與船隻自此脫離中央，李子通的吳國成了江淮第一個有帝號的割據政權，把杜伏威的游擊隊、陳稜的舊防區與宇文化及西去時的散兵重新洗牌。第二層是對唐的雙重示範：李子通在隋末的表現，說明地方武力一旦取得鹽利與舟師就能自立，不必像瓦崗那樣靠劫掠維持；同時他依附、脫離、再自立的歷程，也讓唐高祖看清了招撫、受封、入朝這條路——給名號、給官銜、給宿衛的位置，換取地方軍頭交出兵權。杜伏威622年入朝、輔公祏623年反唐被平，正與李子通的下場互相印證。第三層是長遠的：隋朝崩潰後，河北有竇建德、江淮有杜伏威與李子通、洛陽有王世充，四方把隋的精騎、府庫與漕運分割殆盡；而李子通卒於622年、他建立的吳國在他身後隨即分崩，部眾或降唐或散為流寇，這使唐朝平定江淮幾乎不必再打大仗，只需接管地方、收編船戶。對後世而言，這場起義的意義不在戰術奇謀，而在它示範了隋末地方軍頭化的完整路徑：從漁民、群盜、附軍、自立、稱帝到入朝，短短七年走完全程。
impactEn: There are two layers of direct effect. The first is the map of power in the Huai region. Jiangdu falling in 619 meant the Sui lost the hinge of its southern grain traffic and the city that guarded it at the same time, and the grain, salt and boats of the south slipped out of central control. Li Zitong's Wu became the first southern regime in that region to bear an imperial title, and it reshuffled Du Fuwei's bands of irregulars, Chen Leng's old defence zone and the scattered soldiers left behind by Yuwen Huaji's flight to the west. The second layer is what the war taught the Tang. What Li Zitong showed in the late Sui was that a local armed force, once it had the salt pans and the boats, could stand on its own without the constant plunder that kept the Wagang armies alive; and his own course of attaching, leaving and then standing alone showed the Tang court the road of pacification: hand out titles, offices and a place in the palace guard, and in exchange get the local commanders to give up their troops. Du Fuwei's journey to the capital in 622 and the suppression of Fu Gongshi's revolt in 623 confirm that pattern from the other side. In the longer term the Sui collapse left the empire's cavalry, reserves and grain traffic carved up among Dou Jiande in Hebei, Du Fuwei and Li Zitong in the Huai, and Wang Shichong at Luoyang; and when Li Zitong died in 622 and the state of Wu fell apart behind him, with his men either surrendering to the Tang or scattering as bandits, the Tang's pacification of the Huai required few great battles — only the transfer of authority and the enrolment of boat households. For posterity the significance of this rising lies less in any tactical subtlety than in the complete path it demonstrates of the late-Sui local commander: fisherman, bandit, retainer, independent ruler, emperor, courtier, the whole circuit walked in seven years.
result: 以615年第一次舉兵算起，到622年李子通卒於長安，這場起義前後歷時約七年。結局分三段看：起義本身沒有被撲滅，反而是這一支最後建立了有年號的割據政權——武德二年克江都、自稱皇帝、國號吳、年號明政，時間雖短，卻是江淮第一個名號完整的政權；它也沒有能統一天下，先後受杜伏威與竇建德兩面擠壓，620年幾乎失守，靠向唐請援、等到秦叔寶在泗州毀掉竇建德的舟師才保住江都，此後不過是在唐、杜、竇三方之間勉力維持；最後是人亡政息：武德五年李子通死於長安，吳國群龍無首，所部先後由將領率領歸唐，江淮的割據局面在唐平定竇建德、杜伏威之後徹底結束。必須說明的是，本役的文獻極為有限：《隋書》沒有為李子通立傳，資治通鑑與《舊唐書》《新唐書》各只留下數條散記，兵員、戰損、攻城細節一概無數可對。能夠確定的只有上述幾個節點：615年前後在山東起兵、受杜伏威部、與左才相合而終為所忌、619年破陳稜克江都建吳、620年向唐乞援、622年卒於長安。剩下的空白，只能以同時代江淮諸部與河北義軍的共同處境來補，而不能當成實錄。
resultEn: Counting from the first raising of men in 615 to Li Zitong's death at Chang'an in 622, the rising ran about seven years. Its outcome reads in three parts. It was not put down; this force was the one that in the end built a regime with a calendar of its own — taking Jiangdu in 619, proclaiming himself emperor, founding the state of Wu and the era Mingzheng. It was short-lived, but it was the first complete political title in the Huai region. Nor did it unify anything. Squeezed from both sides by Du Fuwei and Dou Jiande, it nearly fell in 620 and was saved only by begging the Tang for aid and waiting until Qin Shubao destroyed Dou Jiande's fleet near Si prefecture, after which Jiangdu was held and nothing more than a stubborn existence between the Tang on one side and Du and Dou on the other could be maintained. Finally, the man died and the polity dissolved: in 622 Li Zitong died at Chang'an, the state of Wu lost its centre, and his troops were led in by their own officers to surrender to the Tang, after which the southern separatist question was closed for good as the Tang destroyed Dou Jiande and absorbed Du Fuwei. It must be said that the record of this war is very thin. The History of Sui gives Li Zitong no biography; the Comprehensive Mirror and the Old and New Tang histories each keep only a few scattered notices; and there are no figures at all for troops, losses or the details of the sieges. What can be fixed is only the sequence above: rising in Shandong around 615, service under Du Fuwei, partnership with Zuo Caixiang and the jealousy that ended it, the defeat of Chen Leng and the taking of Jiangdu in 619, the appeal to Tang in 620, and death at Chang'an in 622. The gaps can only be filled from the shared situation of the other southern and Hebei insurgents of the time, and must not be treated as record.
